title: Stationary write in a backward zipper
statement: Let $A$ be an alphabet, $S$ a set of states, and $x$ a finite input word over $A$. For any optional state $q$, state $q'\in S$, input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ allowed positions, integer frontier $z$, finite lists $l,r$ of possibly blank symbols, output word, and possibly blank symbol $b$, applying the action that writes $b$ and leaves the work head stationary produces the backward-sweep configuration with state $q'$, input-head position $p$, frontier $z$, left list $l$, and right list $b::r.tail$, with the output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: An optional state $q$ and state $q'\in S$
An input-head position $p$ among the $|x|+2$ allowed positions
replaced:
In a backward-facing zipper configuration (work head at cell $z$, a list $r$ occupying
cells $z, z-1, \dots$, a list $l$ occupying cells $z+1, z+2, \dots$), applying the sweep
action that writes a symbol $b$ at the current cell without moving, leaves the input
head and output unchanged, and enters a state $q'$ replaces the first entry of $r$ by
$b$ and the control state by $q'$, leaving everything else fixed.
